## Independent re-measurement of the #5393 cost model

Re-measured from scratch against the raw REST API (`api.github.com`, `curl` + token), not
through a wrapper, with every load-bearing figure taken from **unfiltered** reads and every
elapsed computed from the **jobs' own** `started_at` / `completed_at`. Current time was read
from the API `Date` response header rather than assumed — a mistake I made once mid-run and
caught, which is exactly the failure mode this card names.

Samples (all unfiltered `GET /actions/workflows/{file}/runs`, then classified locally):

| set | n | window |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` runs, all events | 1200 | 2026-08-12T00:05:51Z .. 2026-08-20T09:58:23Z |
| of those, `push`/`main` | 378 | same |
| jobs fetched for those | 2238 | same |
| `ci.yml` `pull_request` runs sampled | 220 (133 with 4 real shards) | 2026-08-18 .. 2026-08-20 |
| `changeset-release.yml` runs | 400 (200 with jobs fetched) | 2026-08-12T04:23Z .. 2026-08-20T09:58Z |

### Verdict table

| # | claim | verdict | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | full suite runs twice per merge, unsharded, overlapping | **confirmed** | shards `skipped` in 121/121 push runs; `Test (coverage)` present in 121/121; 89/89 commit pairs overlap in wall clock, median overlap 11m09s |
| 2 | 39 min / 34 min / 9m47s | **confirmed as magnitudes, corrected as statistics** | coverage 37m32s median (3-day, n=35); release `Run tests` 31m14s median (n=104); PR slowest shard 9m17s median (n=133) |
| 3 | `Test (coverage)` is 34 s from its 40-min cap | **confirmed, and stronger than claimed** | the cap has **already fired 4 times**; 21/35 recent runs land within 3 min of it |
| 4 | `concurrency` without `cancel-in-progress` makes runs wait ~35 min | **mechanism confirmed, magnitude refuted** | median wait 5m08s, not ~35 min; 22% of release wall clock is waiting, not half; and 95/200 runs never ran at all |
| 5 | most `push`/`main` CI runs end `cancelled` | **confirmed** | 271/378 = 71.7% cancelled; only 28.3% reach a verdict |

Everything below shows the method for each.

---

## Claim 1 — the suite really does run twice per merge, in parallel — CONFIRMED

Static side, from `main`:

- `ci.yml` `test` (the 4 shards) carries `if: github.event_name != 'push'`.
- `ci.yml` `test-coverage` carries `if: github.event_name == 'push'` and `timeout-minutes: 40`.
- `changeset-release.yml` runs `pnpm test`; root `package.json` has `"test": "vitest run"` — unsharded.

Measured side, over the 124 `push`/`main` runs in the recent window (121 of which produced jobs;
3 were cancelled before any job existed):

| | result |
|---|---|
| runs where the shard matrix is present but `skipped` | 121/121 |
| runs containing a `Test (coverage)` job | 121/121 |
| `pull_request` runs where `Test (coverage)` is present but `skipped` | 153/153 |

So the two lanes are exactly complementary, as the YAML says.

**Do they overlap, or does one gate the other?** Pairing the two lanes by `head_sha` gives 89
commits where both lanes produced a real test execution. **89/89 overlap in wall clock** —
median overlap 11m09s, max 37m41s, and not one pair where the release job started only after
the coverage job had finished. 86/89 pairs were even created at the identical push timestamp.
Neither gates the other; they are two independent full runs of the same suite on the same commit.

Most recent pair, run [32356587040](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32356587040) and [32356587006](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32356587006), sha `59f61cfb8`:

```
CI  Test (coverage): 2026-08-20T09:58:43Z -> 2026-08-20T10:38:09Z   39m26s  failure
Rel pnpm test      : 2026-08-20T10:17:46Z -> 2026-08-20T10:51:01Z   33m15s  failure
overlap: 20m23s
```

---

## Claim 2 — the durations — CONFIRMED as magnitudes, CORRECTED as statistics

Each figure in #5393 is a real observation, but each sits at a different point of its
distribution, and one of the three distributions is **moving**.

| lane | claimed | measured median | spread | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` `Test (coverage)` job | ~39 min | **37m32s** (last 3 days) | min 22m13s, p25 35m43s, p75 38m46s, max 39m47s | 35 |
| `ci.yml` `Test (coverage)` job | | 32m42s (last 8 days) | p10 27m27s, p90 38m21s | 109 |
| release `Run tests` step | ~34 min | **31m14s** | job total 33m18s median | 104 |
| PR lane, slowest of 4 shards | 9m47s | **9m17s** | p10 8m51s, p90 9m39s, **p95 9m45s**, max 10m30s | 133 |

- 39 min for the coverage job sits between p75 and p90 of the current window — high, but not
  an outlier, and see claim 3.
- 9m47s for the PR lane is the **p95**, not the median. The median is 9m17s. Both numbers are
  right; only the word "typical" would be wrong.
- Cancelled jobs are excluded from every duration above. A cancelled job's elapsed is a
  truncation, not a duration. Including all 121 recent coverage jobs rather than the 35 that
  finished puts the median at **16m44s** instead of 37m32s — less than half — so this choice is
  load-bearing, not cosmetic.

Per-step medians, which settle a side question from #5393:

| step | `Test (coverage)` | PR shard | release job |
|---|---|---|---|
| the test step itself | **37m10s** | 8m20s | **31m14s** |
| everything else combined | 0m25s | 0m29s | 1m33s |
| `Install dependencies` alone | 0m06s | 0m06s | 0m06s |

`pnpm install` is 6 seconds. #5393's "caching is not the problem" is confirmed with a larger
sample: fixed overhead on a runner in this repo is 25-29 s total.

That also prices sharding on its own, without coverage: 4 shards at 8m20s = 33m20s of runner
time versus 31m14s unsharded — **sharding the plain suite costs about 7% more runner minutes
and returns 3.7x in wall clock.**

---

## Claim 3 — the timeout margin — CONFIRMED, and the situation is past the point the claim describes

#5393 says the job is "34 seconds away from its own timeout". That understates it.
**The 40-minute cap has already fired four times**, and GitHub says so in its own words.

| run | job elapsed | GitHub annotation |
|---|---|---|
| [32350122311](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32350122311) | 40m11s | `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 40m0s` |
| [32333429757](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32333429757) | 40m16s | same |
| [32328584507](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32328584507) | 40m04s | same |
| [32280945493](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32280945493) | 40m06s | same |

These surface in the API as `conclusion: cancelled`, which is why a scan for `failure` misses
them. **They are not `cancel-in-progress` kills**, and that was checked rather than assumed:
`cancel-in-progress` can only fire when a newer `push`/`main` run exists, and for each of the
four the next newer run was created *after* the job had already ended (by 19m00s, 187m18s,
38m57s and 0m11s respectively). A genuine `cancel-in-progress` kill looks different — e.g. run
32355187526's coverage job ran 16m53s and ended 16 s after the newer run was created.

Distribution against the cap, over the 35 coverage jobs that ran to completion in the last 3 days:

| | count |
|---|---|
| within 3 min of the cap (37m00s or longer) | **21/35 (60%)** |
| within 5 min of the cap (35m00s or longer) | 27/35 (77%) |
| past the cap (timeout kills, counted separately) | 4 |

So: **typical, not outlier.** And the reason is visible in the trend — the job's duration is
growing about a minute and a quarter per day:

| day | median completed duration | max | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-12 | 28m44s | 30m07s | 16 |
| 2026-08-13 | 30m12s | 32m57s | 17 |
| 2026-08-14 | 32m17s | 33m37s | 7 |
| 2026-08-15 | 32m42s | 34m40s | 14 |
| 2026-08-16 | 34m07s | 35m38s | 13 |
| 2026-08-17 | 35m56s | 37m48s | 14 |
| 2026-08-18 | 36m57s | 39m17s | 13 |
| 2026-08-19 | 38m24s | 39m14s | 12 |
| 2026-08-20 | **39m32s** | 39m47s | 3 |

The PR lane over the same days moves far less (9m12s, 9m21s, 9m40s), so this is mostly the
coverage lane's own growth, not a general runner slowdown. **Inference, labelled as such:** at
this slope the median crosses 40 min within about a day, and the four timeouts above are the
leading edge of that, not bad luck.

---

## Claim 4 — release queueing — MECHANISM CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE REFUTED

First, the card's methodological warning is confirmed exactly: across all 105 executed release
runs, `run_started_at` minus `created_at` is **0 seconds in 105/105 cases**, including runs
that waited 35 minutes. The run-level field does not expose the wait; the job's `created_at`
does.

Measured with the job's own `created_at`, over the 104 release jobs that ran to completion:

| | median | mean | min | max | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| queue wait (`run.created_at` to `job.created_at`) | **5m08s** | 9m15s | 0m00s | 35m50s | 26m08s |
| executing (`job.started_at` to `job.completed_at`) | **33m18s** | 32m39s | 19m54s | 37m56s | 35m37s |
| total | 38m02s | 41m57s | 19m57s | **70m52s** | 57m25s |

Aggregate: **962 minutes waiting against 3395 minutes executing — 22% of release wall clock is
queueing**, not half. 72/104 runs waited more than 60 s.

#5393's specific example reproduces exactly (run 32350122326: waited 35m23s, executed 35m27s,
70.9 min total) — but that is the **maximum** of the sample, not the typical case. The sentence
"the 70.9 min total is half pure queueing" is true of that run and false of the lane.

**And the model behind the claim is wrong in a way that matters.** #5393 says "each merge
inherits the backlog of the ones before it". It does not. `concurrency` without
`cancel-in-progress` keeps at most **one** run pending per group; a newer arrival cancels the
*pending* one, never the running one. So the lane is a one-slot server with a one-slot waiting
room, and merges arriving when both are occupied are **dropped**, not queued.

Two independent predictions, both hold at 100%:

- **95 of 200** release runs have no job record at all — they never executed anything. Every
  one is `cancelled`, and **95/95** were cancelled within 90 s of the *next* run's creation
  (typically 1-2 s). Example: run 32326250013 created 02:53:28Z, cancelled 02:56:45Z; the next
  run was created 02:56:44Z.
- **0 of 104** adjacent executed release jobs overlap in time.

Consequence for the ruling: the release lane does not have an unbounded backlog to drain, so
"stop spending 34 of the 35 minutes on tests" would cut the 33m18s execution and most of the
5m08s median wait, but it would not be recovering a 35-minute queue on every merge.

⚠️ #5393's warning against `cancel-in-progress: true` on this workflow **stands and is
reinforced** by the above: the runs currently being cancelled are the *pending* ones, which have
published nothing. `cancel-in-progress: true` would start cancelling the *running* one, whose
last step is `changeset publish`.

---

## Claim 5 — cancellation — CONFIRMED

Unfiltered, 378 `push`/`main` `ci.yml` runs over 8 days:

| conclusion | n | share |
|---|---|---|
| cancelled | 271 | **71.7%** |
| success | 56 | 14.8% |
| failure | 51 | 13.5% |

Only **28.3%** of push-lane runs reach a verdict at all. At job level for `Test (coverage)`
specifically: 264 cancelled / 58 success / 51 failure — a verdict in **29.2%** of runs.

Narrowed to the last 3 days (n=124): 73.4% cancelled, 33 failures, and **zero successes**.
A lane that is cancelled 7 times out of 10 is not providing the coverage its existence implies —
confirmed. The next section shows it is worse than that.

---

## Findings neither #5393 nor this card anticipated

### A. ⚠️ `Test (coverage)` has not passed since 2026-08-16, and Codecov has had nothing since

This is the finding I would put in front of the maintainer first, because it changes what the
job is worth.

| | |
|---|---|
| last successful `Test (coverage)` job | **2026-08-16T10:56:13Z**, run [31942979071](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/31942979071) |
| last successful `Upload coverage to Codecov` step | **the same run** — 58/373 coverage jobs ever reached it in the window, none after that one |
| completed coverage jobs since | 51, **all failures**, 0 successes |

The `Upload coverage to Codecov` step has no `if:`, so it carries the implicit `success()` and
is `skipped` whenever the test step fails — it is `skipped` in 311 of 373 coverage jobs and in
**120 of the 121** most recent ones. So the entire justification in `ci.yml`'s comment —
*"one unsharded run so Codecov still receives a single complete report"* — has been delivering
nothing for four days.

**And it is one test.** Reading GitHub's check-run annotations for every one of those jobs:

| failing test file | occurrences among the 51 completed failures |
|---|---|
| `scripts/__tests__/check-package-self-import.test.ts` | **50** |
| `scripts/__tests__/quick-reference-current-release-4143.test.ts` | 3 |
| three others (one run, 2026-08-17) | 1 each |

The message is always the same:

```
[unit] scripts/__tests__/check-package-self-import.test.ts
  > a package name that is not a module edge is not a finding
  > the two live specimens in this repository stay unflagged
Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
  at scripts/__tests__/check-package-self-import.test.ts:140:3
```

First occurrence 2026-08-16T12:48:02Z — one run after the last green one at 10:56Z. Present in
every completed failure since.

**It does not fail on the PR lane.** Same method, same annotation API, over the failing PR shard
jobs in the same window: `check-package-self-import.test.ts` appears **0 times**. Counter-probe
for that zero, because a zero is not a reading: the identical scan over the identical jobs does
return annotations — 7 of them, naming `vite-alias-closure.test.ts`,
`AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx`, `vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts`,
`check-type-check-coverage.test.ts` and `check-changeset-no-major.test.ts` — and the same call
against the push lane returns 50 hits for the file in question. The method works; the zero is real.

**Inference, labelled as such:** this is a 15-second per-test budget being crossed under v8
coverage instrumentation — the exact shape AGENTS.md describes under
"flaky 测试:先找竞态,别调超时", where an unbounded cost lands inside a bounded window. It is
not a `main`-content bug and it is *not* #5394: the `QUICK_REFERENCE.md` drift appears in 3 of
373 coverage jobs, all recent; this one has been there for four days.

**Sharding would not fix this — measured by ablation.** The prototype run gives the third cell
of the table, so the discriminator can be identified rather than guessed:

| lane | sharded? | v8 coverage? | does `check-package-self-import` time out? |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR lane, production, 220 runs sampled | yes, 4 ways | no | **no** — 0 occurrences |
| push lane, production, 373 coverage jobs | no | yes | **yes** — 50 of 51 completed failures |
| prototype run 32364577842, same commit | yes, 4 ways | yes | **yes** — present in the merged report, and shards 3 and 4 exited 1 |

Holding coverage on and varying sharding changes nothing; holding sharding on and varying
coverage flips it. **The v8 instrumentation is what pushes that test past its 15-second budget,
not the size of the run.** So sharding the coverage job buys the wall clock and the timeout
margin, but it does **not** make the lane green — that test needs its own fix either way.

Two consequences for the ruling on #5393:

1. Proposal 2's "either shard it or run it daily" is not just a cost decision — **whichever is
   chosen has to make this test pass**, or Codecov stays dark either way.
2. The argument for proposal 1 ("the CI push lane still runs the whole suite") is weaker than it
   reads: the push lane currently reaches a verdict in 29% of runs and that verdict has been
   `failure` every time for four days. The release job's `pnpm test` is, right now, the only
   post-merge full-suite run that ever comes back green.

### B. The merge cadence in #5393 is roughly 2.7x low

#5393 assumes "roughly 18 merges to `main` in a working day". Every push to `main` creates
exactly one `Changeset Release` run (that workflow has no `paths-ignore`), so counting those
runs counts pushes:

| day | pushes to `main` |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-13 | 57 |
| 2026-08-14 | 13 |
| 2026-08-15 | 41 |
| 2026-08-16 | 49 |
| 2026-08-17 | 74 |
| 2026-08-18 | 76 |
| 2026-08-19 | 36 |

Median **49/day**. And only 2 of the 400 sampled pushes are the changesets bot's own
`chore: release packages` commit, so this is real merge traffic, not the release lane feeding
itself. Any per-day saving estimate in #5393 should be scaled accordingly.

Billed runner time actually consumed by the two post-merge suite runs, summing real job
durations rather than modelling: **96.2 runner-hours over ~2.7 days, about 36 runner-hours per
day** — and that is *with* 71% of coverage jobs being cancelled early. Nominal cost if they all
ran to completion is 68m24s of test-step time per merge.

### C. #5393's account of its own false finding is not reproducible

The card asks me not to inherit the PM's mistake, so I tried to reproduce it. The retraction in
#5393 attributes the wrong Aug-7 figure to the filter combination `branch=main` + `event=push` +
`status=completed` returning a stale newest result. **That query is not stale.** Run against raw
REST just now:

```
branch=main&event=push&status=completed  -> total_count=3847, newest 2026-08-20T09:58:23Z
```

correctly ordered, newest first. The same filters through the MCP Actions wrapper return the same
newest run. I probed each `status` value one at a time (`success`, `failure`, `cancelled`,
`in_progress`, `queued`, `waiting`, `action_required`, `neutral`, `timed_out`, `skipped`,
`stale`) and **none** yields 2026-08-07 as the newest result.

So the finding was indeed false, but the stated cause is unverified. What *is* verified is the
remedy the card prescribes: the unfiltered read cross-checks correctly every time, and it is what
caught this. Worth recording so the next agent does not "avoid the stale filter" and think itself
safe.

One incidental oddity found while probing, reported because it is the same class of trap:
`status=queued` returns `total_count: 1` with an **empty** result page. A count is not a reading
either.

### D. `Test (coverage)` failing does not turn the check red for anything

Not a new claim, just confirmation of the premise both other cards rest on: 89/89 pairs show the
two lanes running concurrently and independently, `ci.yml`'s push lane is not judged by branch
protection or the merge queue (its own comment says so), and 271/378 push runs are cancelled
mid-flight with no consequence. Nothing blocks on it — which is what makes four days of red go
unnoticed.

---

## Pricing the sharded-coverage option — measured, not modelled

`ci.yml`'s comment declines sharding the coverage job because it *"isn't worth the blob report
merge"*. I built the sharded version on a throwaway branch and ran it against the unsharded
production recipe **on the same commit, in the same run, on the same runner class**, so the
comparison has no day-to-day drift in it.

Branch `claude/issue-5395-ci-cost-model-verification`, commit `6a4b435e4` (a checkout of
`main` at `59f61cfb8` plus the throwaway instrument), run
[32364577842](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32364577842):

| job | test step | job wall clock |
|---|---|---|
| unsharded coverage — the production recipe verbatim | 38m40s | **39m05s** |
| sharded coverage 1/4 | 10m16s | 10m46s |
| sharded coverage 2/4 | 10m45s | **11m17s** (slowest) |
| sharded coverage 3/4 | 10m05s | 10m34s |
| sharded coverage 4/4 | 8m47s | 9m16s |
| merge the 4 blob reports | **0m13s** | 0m47s |

**The price:**

| | unsharded (today) | 4-way sharded | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| wall clock (critical path) | 39m05s | **12m04s** | **3.24x faster, 27m01s saved per merge** |
| runner minutes | 39m05s | 42m40s | **+9.2%** |
| the "blob report merge" | n/a | 13 s of compute, 47 s of job | — |

Against the 3-day production median of 37m32s rather than this one baseline, it is still 3.11x
and 25m28s saved.

**Reproduced.** A second run on the same commit
([32368063518](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32368063518)) measured the
four shards at 10m46s / 11m13s / 9m23s / 8m31s — slowest 11m13s against run 1's 11m17s — and its
unsharded arms at 39m25s and 40m13s. Two independent samples, same answer.

**So the cost the comment declines to pay is 13 seconds.** The merge is
`vitest run --merge-reports --coverage`; the shards are the existing command plus
`--reporter=blob --shard=N/4`. The `~26% more runner minutes` the comment predicts for sharding
measures 9.2% here, because coverage makes the per-shard work larger relative to the fixed
25-second runner overhead.

Sharding also moves the job to a comfortable distance from any timeout — the slowest shard is
11m17s against `timeout-minutes: 20` on the existing shard job.

### Does the merged report stay equivalent for Codecov? — yes, no dropped files

Run 1 could not answer this: the unsharded arm produced **no coverage file at all**. So run 2
([32368063518](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32368063518)) puts both
arms through the *identical* blob-plus-merge path, so the only difference between the two
reports is one process versus four.

| | unsharded, 1 process | 4 shards merged | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| files in the report | **1287** | **1287** | **0 — `onlyUnsharded=0`, `onlyMerged=0`** |
| statements | 55432/84590 = 65.5302% | 55395/84590 = 65.4865% | -37 hits, **-0.0437 pp** |
| functions | 11593/18972 = 61.1058% | 11589/18972 = 61.0848% | -4 hits, -0.0211 pp |
| branches | 47720/80165 = 59.5272% | 47695/80165 = 59.4960% | -25 hits, -0.0312 pp |
| files with fewer covered statements after merging | — | **3** | `DirectoryPage.tsx` 6 to 3, `ResourceEditPage.tsx` 464 to 431, `AuthProvider.tsx` 193 to 192 |

**No file is dropped**, and the totals move by four hundredths of a percentage point against
thresholds set at 40/33/30/40. For a trend signal that is immaterial.

Is the 37-statement gap sharding, or noise? I have a noise floor, because the two prototype runs
each produced a merged 4-shard report from the same commit: statements 55398 vs 55395, functions
11591 vs 11589, branches 47694 vs 47695 — so an identical configuration wanders by about 3 hits
between runs. The unsharded-versus-sharded gap is roughly ten times that, so **a small systematic
difference is likely real**, concentrated in three files (one of them, `ResourceEditPage.tsx`,
accounts for 33 of the 37). **Inference, labelled as such:** those look like files whose covering
tests land in different shards and no longer share a module instance. It does not lose files and
it does not move the reported percentage meaningfully, but it is not bit-identical and should not
be described as such.

### ⚠️ Reproduced: the live unsharded recipe writes no coverage report at all when the suite fails

Both prototype runs, on the same commit, with the production command
`pnpm test:coverage --coverage.reporter=json --coverage.reporter=text`:

| run | job | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 32364577842 | unsharded live, 39m05s | `NO COVERAGE FILE at coverage/coverage-final.json` |
| 32368063518 | unsharded live, 39m25s | `NO coverage/ DIRECTORY AT ALL after the live unsharded run` |

Two for two. Meanwhile the blob-plus-merge path produced a full report from the same tree with
the same failing tests, every time.

So there are **two independent reasons** Codecov has received nothing since 2026-08-16, not one:
the `Upload coverage to Codecov` step is `skipped` by its implicit `success()`, **and** on this
evidence there would have been no file for it to upload anyway. As long as the suite is red, the
current job cannot produce a coverage report at all.

### Incidental, from the same run

`PROTO unsharded via blob` took **40m13s** and the live arm 39m25s — on a checkout of `main`, on
an ordinary runner, both at or past the production job's `timeout-minutes: 40`. That is claim 3
reproducing outside the production lane.

The blob reports themselves are small: 4 artifacts of 5.86-5.99 MiB, uploaded in 3 s each and
downloaded in 4 s; the merged `coverage-final.json` is 3.83 MiB. Adding those to the 13 s merge
step, the total price of "the blob report merge" that `ci.yml` declines is **under a minute**.
---

## What I could not measure

- **Actions job logs and artifacts.** Both redirect to `productionresultssa12.blob.core.windows.net`,
